samples.summary: Pasted `href` is still stored unvalidated, and this delta finalises Clear formatting as no longer stripping it — defence now rests entirely on the navigation/export-time gates
samples.evidence: Vector: attacker gets a victim to paste HTML containing `<a href="javascript:...">` (clipboard.ts:611 and the sibling path at clipboard.ts:713 assign `el.getAttribute('href')` to `style.href` with no `isSafeUrl` check), so an unsafe scheme is persisted into the Yorkie document and syncs to every collaborator. Before this PR, `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` included `href`, so Clear formatting was one blunt user-reachable way to scrub such a run; this delta cements the opposite (`types.ts` doc now says `href` is preserved; `text-editor.ts:3435-3447` only re-arms the trailing-edge exit) and compensates with a Remove-link button. I could NOT complete the chain to execution: every consumer I traced gates the value — Ctrl/Cmd+click `window.open` gates on `isSafeUrl` (text-editor.ts:1822), the view-only click path gates at text-editor.ts:2176, the popover anchor gates at docs-link-popover.tsx:217/224, PDF export gates via `isEmittableAnnotationUri` (pdf-painter.ts:854), markdown export via `isEmittableMarkdownUrl` (markdown.ts:384), PPTX export via `isExportableHref` (slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:333), and PPTX import allowlists schemes (slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:556-570); slides has no click-to-open path at all. So this is defence-in-depth (unsafe value stored and now harder for a user to remove), not a live XSS. Sanitising at the paste boundary would remove the reliance on every future consumer remembering the gate.
